buyer_decision: How much virgin material a one-material recovery loop will still need over a planning horizon at a chosen recovery fraction, and what secondary stock to plan storage for.
proven: For demand D >= 0, recovery fraction r in [0,1] and stock retention rho in [0,1), the virgin input per period D(1 - r) lies between 0 and D; the secondary stock gap to r D / (1 - rho) shrinks as rho^t and the stock converges to that level; the virgin total over T periods is T D (1 - r); and for D > 0, T > 0 that total strictly falls as r rises.
assumed: One material; demand, recovery fraction and retention are constant over the horizon; recovery is not capped by the stock actually available; no quality losses, rebound demand or price effects; the numbers supplied are the real ones.
